title: Government’s Position on Court Ruling to Award Adoption to Man in Same-sex Relationship
what_it_is: Government’s Position on Court Ruling to Award Adoption to Man in Same-sex Relationship

sections.label: Questions on same-sex adoption ruling
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister about the Ministry's position on a High Court adoption ruling, related policies, and banning commercial surrogacy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development what is the Ministry's position on the recent High Court ruling to award adoption to a single man in a same-sex relationship, of his biological child born through an overseas surrogacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development what implications there are with regard to other Government policies, including education and housing, that need to be reviewed given the recent High Court ruling to award adoption to a single man in a same-sex relationship, of his biological son conceived through a surrogacy done overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will (i) ban commercial surrogacy in Singapore, (ii) prohibit agreements to pay for surrogacy in Singapore or overseas and (iii) disallow adoptions arising from commercial surrogacy whether such surrogacy occurs in Singapore or overseas.

sections.label: High Court allowed adoption
sections.summary: In December 2018, a High Court of three judges allowed the adoption to proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In December 2018, the High Court, which comprised three judges, allowed the adoption to proceed.

sections.label: MSF opposes homosexual parent family units
sections.summary: MSF does not support family units with children and homosexual parents through adoption, and did not support the couple's appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: However, we do not support the formation of family units with children and homosexual parents, through institutions and processes, such as adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Therefore, MSF did not support the appeal by the homosexual couple to adopt the child that they had conceived through surrogacy overseas, after they had been informed that the Government would not support the application to adopt the child because this would have been contrary to public policy.

sections.label: MSF reviewing adoption laws
sections.summary: The Court allowed the child's adoption, and MSF is reviewing adoption laws and practices to better reflect public policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Based on the specific facts of this case, the Court allowed the appeal to allow the child to be adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Following the Court's judgment, MSF is reviewing our adoption laws and practices to see how they should be strengthened to better reflect public policy which, in turn, is a reflection of the values of our broad society today.

sections.label: Prior surrogacy adoptions and benefits
sections.summary: Courts previously granted adoption of 10 children born abroad through surrogacy; adoption does not guarantee citizenship, education or housing benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Prior to this, the Courts have granted adoption of 10 children born abroad as a result of surrogacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: While an adoption order serves to make a child legitimate under the law, it does not on its own guarantee benefits and privileges, such as citizenship, education or housing.

sections.label: Surrogacy not allowed in Singapore
sections.summary: Due to ethical and practical concerns, surrogacy is not permissible at Singapore healthcare institutions and is not allowed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Because of the ethical considerations and the practical concerns about surrogacy, it is not permissible currently in Singapore to be carried out at healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, our position currently, as it stands, is that we do not allow it in Singapore.

sections.label: Minister considering Member's route
sections.summary: The Minister says all the Member's suggestions will be considered as part of the overall review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider that as a route?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will take all the Member's suggestions into consideration as part of this overall review.
